overview.summary: Translators change written text from one language into another so that its meaning, tone and purpose are kept. Interpreters do the same for speech.
overview.problems: They help people, businesses and governments communicate across languages.
overview.worksWith: Clients, project managers, editors, subject experts and other translators.
overview.workplaces: Translation agencies, companies, international organizations, publishers and courts, and many translators work freelance from home.

timeline.title: Read the brief and the source text
timeline.description: The translator checks the subject, audience and style and reads the whole text first.
timeline.why: Understanding the whole text prevents wrong choices.

timeline.title: Research terms
timeline.description: The translator looks up specialized words, names and style guides.

timeline.title: Translating
timeline.description: The translator writes the translation, keeping the meaning, tone and style natural in the target language.
timeline.why: A good translation reads as if it were written in that language.

timeline.title: Checking and editing
timeline.description: The translator reads the translation on its own, compares it with the original and fixes errors.

timeline.title: Client communication
timeline.description: The translator asks questions, delivers on time and handles feedback.

timeline.title: Deadlines and big projects
timeline.description: Urgent texts can mean long hours.
timeline.why: Clients often need translations by fixed dates.

responsibilities: Keeping up with both languages and their subject fields
challenges: Income can be uneven for freelancers.
Rates can be low because of competition and machine translation.
Some texts are difficult, technical or emotionally heavy.
The work means long hours at a computer.
Specializing in a field such as legal or medical text usually needs extra training.
Keeping both languages fresh takes continuous effort.
skills: Excellent knowledge of at least two languages
workEnvironment: Mostly desk and computer based, at home, in agencies or in organizations. Freelancers manage their own clients, rates and schedule. Interpreters work in meetings, courts or events and may travel.
tradeoffs: Pay that varies by language, field and country

activity.title: Translate a short paragraph and have it checked
steps: Write an 80-word paragraph about something simple, such as your day, in a language you know well.
Translate it into another language you are learning or know.
Underline words that did not translate directly and note how you handled them.
Ask a speaker of that language, such as a teacher or friend, to read it and say whether it sounds natural.
Revise it and note whether the careful word work felt interesting.
activity.outcome: You practise choosing words for meaning, not just word for word, and using feedback.
activity.safety: Use only your own writing, not copyrighted texts, and do not share personal information in what you translate or ask others to check.

source: Written by Futurixia from general knowledge of how this profession works. It is illustrative and is not based on interviews or surveys.
